name: Chimakum
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Boas 1892, Notes on the Chemakum Language, American Anthropologist 5:37-44 (cited on Wikipedia 'Chemakum language'; full text not reachable, archive.org 503)
earlier_scan.note: Boas 1892 is the only substantive description; also Powell 1974 word lists.

sources.citation: Andrade, Manuel J. 1953. Notes on the Relations between Chemakum and Quileute. International Journal of American Linguistics 19(3): 212-215 (Glottolog lists 212-255; the article occupies pp. 212-215 in the issue scan).
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Sound-correspondence notes only; no stress rule for Chemakum. p. 215: the less uniform correspondences 'seem to depend on position in the word, the surrounding sounds, and possibly accent'; Sapir's marginal note printed as fn 3 (p. 214): 'Anything in accent here?'

sources.citation: Boas, Franz. 1892. Notes on the Chemakum Language. American Anthropologist 5(1): 37-44.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online
sources.note: The 'Phonetics' paragraph (pp. 37-38) treats only vowels (obscure vowels frequent, diphthongs ai/au), the consonant inventory and initial/final clusters; nothing on stress or accent. Word forms carry an unexplained acute mark after a vowel (he'na 'my father', o'tltets, ha'maa 'tree', tsu'qot 'lake', helo'le'l 'canoe', hau'atska 'deer'); the footnote key explains only consonant symbols and '!'. No rule stated.

sources.citation: Mithun, Marianne. 1999. The Languages of Native North America. Cambridge: CUP. Excerpt 'Chimakuan family', pp. 378-379 (Rosetta Project extract).
sources.harvard_location: TOZ GEN N.A.LING. M 696 l; WID WID-LC PM108.L35 1999
sources.note: The extract contains only the morphosyntax paragraphs (Quileute data from Andrade 1933); no phonology paragraph and nothing on stress. Survey, not primary.

sources.citation: Swadesh, Morris. 1955. Chemakum Lexicon Compared with Quileute. International Journal of American Linguistics 21(1): 60-72.
sources.note: Introduction (pp. 60-62) reconstructs the Proto-Chemakuan phoneme inventory and evaluates Boas's transcription (glottalization, k/q, vowel length, glottal stop) but says nothing about stress or accent; the normalized Chemakum forms in the lexicon carry no accent marks.

sources.citation: Elmendorf, William W. 1990. Chemakum. Handbook of North American Indians 7 (Northwest Coast): 438-440.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Standard ethnographic chapter; may carry a one-paragraph language note with a pointer to Powell's analysis. Unlikely to state a stress rule.

sources.citation: Powell, James V. 1974. Proto-Chimakuan: Materials for a Reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawaii.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only modern analytic treatment of Chemakum phonology (reinterprets Boas's 1890 notebooks; Wikipedia cites it for the vowel system, p. 16). A reconstruction comparing Chemakum with Quileute, which has contrastive stress, is the work most likely to say what Boas's accent marks mean and whether Chemakum stress was predictable.

sources.citation: Boas, Franz. 1890. Chemakum materials (field notebooks, c. 1,250 items). Franz Boas Collection, American Philosophical Society Library, Philadelphia.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The sole primary corpus of the language; carries Boas's accent marks on every form and any remark he made about accent. Swadesh 1955 fn 2 confirms it is held at the APS.

sources.citation: Boas, Franz. 1890. Chemakum materials (field notebooks); Gibbs, George. Chemakum vocabulary. Manuscripts, Franz Boas Collection, American Philosophical Society Library.
